Guarded AIPW estimator

estimate_beta_aipw_lambda.Rd

Augmented IPW estimator of \(\theta = (\beta, \sigma)\) with a closed-form augmentation \(\Psi_{closed}\) (a working normal model for \(X | Z\) with the mean and standard deviation of the fitted Weibull model for \(X | Z\)) and the matrix \(\Lambda\) that minimizes the asymptotic variance within the class \(\Lambda \Psi_{closed}\). Because of \(\Lambda\), the guarded AIPW estimator is at least as efficient as the IPW estimator asymptotically, whether or not the working model is correct. It is consistent when the model for \(C | (Y, Z)\) and the mean of the outcome model are correctly specified. \(\Lambda\) is estimated once, at the IPW estimate, and held fixed. The sandwich standard errors account for estimating the weights.

Usage

estimate_beta_aipw_lambda(
  data_yXZ,
  model,
  model_xz = NULL,
  model_weights = NULL,
  gamma = NULL,
  aw_var = "AW",
  a_var = "A"
)

Arguments

data_yXZ

A data frame with one row per subject. It must contain the outcome, the covariates in model, the age a_var, the observed W = min(X, C), and the indicator D = I(X <= C).

model

A formula for the outcome model, y ~ AW + Z1 + ..., with the time-to-event covariate aw_var on the right-hand side. The outcome model is \(Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 (A - X) + \beta_Z' Z + \epsilon\), \(\epsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\).

model_xz

A one-sided formula for the Weibull AFT model of \(X | Z\), for example ~ Z. Defaults to the covariates of model other than aw_var.

model_weights

A one-sided formula for the Weibull AFT model of \(C | (Y, Z)\), for example ~ y + Z. Defaults to the outcome and the covariates of model other than aw_var.

gamma

Optional coefficients and scale of the Weibull model for \(X | Z\) that supply the working moments (as in estimate_beta_mle()$gamma_est). If NULL, the joint MLE is fitted first.

aw_var

Name of the column A - W in model. Defaults to "AW".

a_var

Name of the age column A. Defaults to "A".

Value

A list with beta_est, se_est, converged, and Lambda.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
dat <- data_aft(500)
estimate_beta_aipw_lambda(dat, y ~ AW + Z, model_xz = ~ Z, model_weights = ~ y + Z)
#> $beta_est
#> (Intercept)          AW           Z       sigma 
#>   1.0080240   0.9867175   1.0462881   1.0110685 
#> 
#> $se_est
#> (Intercept)          AW           Z       sigma 
#>  0.07687965  0.04860933  0.04905001  0.03510546 
#> 
#> $converged
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $Lambda
#>              (Intercept)          AW           Z       sigma
#> (Intercept)  0.754632028  0.09852326 -0.17964625 0.017292856
#> AW          -0.008584629  0.86019464 -0.06941746 0.088105583
#> Z           -0.148856979  0.10356851  0.85917059 0.005689848
#> sigma        0.449443817 -0.02767799  0.23815761 0.984086077
#> 
# }
